setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. You are trained to care for a portable vacuum using its manufacturer's instructions.
detail: It is the middle of the afternoon.
pressure: {coworker3} says it is not worth the trouble.
You are in a hurry to finish.

tiers.1: A machine that may be failing can hurt someone or break down in use.
tiers.2: Service due dates exist to prevent failures before heavy use.
tiers.3: Routine care keeps equipment efficient and extends its life.
tiers.4: A log is how the next person knows how much use a machine has had.
tiers.5: Good storage protects equipment between jobs.

fact: The portable vacuum has started making a grinding sound, and the maintenance guide says unusual noises are reported before more use.
issues.action: Stop using it and report the noise to {lead|the}.
issues.reason: A new grinding sound can mean a part is failing, and more use can make the damage worse.
issues.lesson: Stop and report a new problem with equipment instead of running it until it fails.

shortcut.text: Keep running it until your shift ends, since it still works.
shortcut.brief: keep running it until your shift ends
shortcut.why: Running a failing part can cause more damage or injury, and the guide says to report first.
shortcut.mis: If it still works, it is fine.

clear: You already stopped the machine and reported the grinding sound.

fact: The sticker on the portable vacuum shows service was due last week, and the guide says overdue equipment is serviced before heavy use.
issues.action: Ask {lead|the} to schedule service before using it for heavy work.
issues.brief: ask for service before heavy use
issues.reason: Service finds small problems before heavy use turns them into failures.
issues.lesson: Get overdue equipment serviced before you ask it to do heavy work.

shortcut.text: Use it for the big job first and schedule service afterward.
shortcut.why: Heavy use is when an overdue machine is most likely to fail, and the guide says to service it first.
shortcut.mis: Service can wait until after the big job.

clear: {Lead|the} already scheduled the overdue service for the machine.
issues.done: the overdue service is already scheduled

fact: You are trained to clean the portable vacuum's filter using its manufacturer's isolation and cleaning instructions, and today it is due.
issues.action: Follow the trained isolation and cleaning procedure for the filter.
issues.reason: A clogged filter makes the motor work harder, which wastes energy and shortens its life.
issues.lesson: Do routine care on schedule, even when the equipment seems fine.

shortcut.text: Skip it this week, since the machine seems fine.
shortcut.why: Problems from a dirty filter build up quietly, and the guide sets weekly cleaning for that reason.
shortcut.mis: If a machine seems fine, care can wait.

clear: The filter was already cleaned this week.

fact: The guide says to log each machine's hours of use, and you just used the portable vacuum for four hours.
issues.short: the unlogged four hours of use
issues.action: Record the four hours in the machine's log.
issues.reason: Hours of use tell the next person when service is due, and only you know your hours.
issues.lesson: Record equipment use so others can plan service.

shortcut.text: Skip the log, since someone else will probably fill it in.
shortcut.why: Nobody else knows your hours, so the record would be wrong or missing.
shortcut.mis: Someone else will take care of it.

clear: The four hours of use were already recorded in the log.

fact: The guide says portable equipment goes back in its case after use, and you have finished with the portable vacuum.
issues.short: the equipment left out after use
issues.action: Clean it and put it back in its case before you leave.
issues.brief: clean it and return it to its case
issues.reason: Equipment stored in its case is protected from knocks, dust and damp between jobs.
issues.lesson: Clean and store equipment properly after each use.

shortcut.text: Leave it out so it is ready for tomorrow.
shortcut.why: Equipment left out gets knocked, dirty or damp, and the guide says to store it in its case.

proceed.text: Carry on with your regular work, since nothing here needs action.
proceed.why: Each of these situations involves equipment care that needs a response.
proceed.lesson: Equipment lasts longer and works better when problems are reported and routine care is done on schedule.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} what they usually do and copy that.
generic.why: A coworker's habit is not the written guide, and it may be out of date.
generic.mis: Common practice is the same as the rule.

generic.text: Wait until {lead|the} brings it up before you act.
generic.why: The guide applies to you now, and waiting leaves the problem in place.
generic.mis: Someone else will raise it if it matters.

overcaution.text: Stop using every machine in the area until each one has been fully serviced.
overcaution.why: The concern is specific. Stopping everything delays work that safe equipment can do.
overcaution.mis: One problem means all equipment is unsafe.

setup: You have finished using a portable vacuum. You are trained to follow its manufacturer's isolation and cleaning instructions before storage.

steps.text: Follow the trained shutdown and isolation procedure
Clean it using the manufacturer's instructions
Put it back in its case

rel: Log the use once it has stopped.
process.lesson: Switch off, clean, store, and log the use.

title: Equipment care reminders
intro: You are checking a reminder sheet before it is posted near the equipment.
prompt: Which line gives advice that would harm the equipment?
doc.lesson: Good equipment care means reporting problems, servicing on time, doing routine care and logging use.

lines.text: Stop and report any new noise from equipment.

bad.text: Keep running equipment that makes a new noise until it stops working.
bad.why: Running a failing part can cause more damage or injury.

lines.text: Service overdue equipment before heavy use.
lines.fine: Prevents failures when they matter most.

bad.text: Do the heavy job first and service overdue equipment afterward.
bad.why: Heavy use is when an overdue machine is most likely to fail.

lines.text: Log your hours of use after each job.

bad.text: Skip the use log when you expect a coworker to fill it in.
bad.why: Only the person who used it knows the hours, so the log would be wrong.

lines.text: Follow the trained isolation and cleaning procedure before storing portable equipment.

review.notes: Equipment care only; no manufacturer or standard is named. Tiers: failing part, overdue service, routine care, logging, storage.
